A dedicated make target keeps the Phase 14 workqueue packet runnable with the same bounded discipline as the rest of the tranche.
The existing export shim already gives Zigux a reviewable kernel namespace foothold for this boundary-study lane.

The bridge records queue_work_on(), __queue_work(), allocation entrypoints, and explicit stay-in-C decisions so the lane stays descriptive rather than pretending to own live worker execution, matching the roadmap's wrapper-first study posture and the freeze map's Study / Boundary Only bucket for kernel/workqueue.c.
The dedicated Zig test keeps the boundary-map packet pinned to the manifest and the survey note.
The slice note records the exact review-only packet so the lane does not drift into fake implementation claims.
The survey note keeps the roadmap framing and the current blocked-maintenance packet honest.
The bridge now carries a review-only audit that names pool->manager, WORK_STRUCT_PENDING_BIT, pwq->refcnt, and pwq->mayday_cursor without claiming live concurrency ownership.
The bridge records the inactive_works gate and keeps workqueue_set_max_active in a review-only posture under the shipped C locking model.
The bridge records the last_pool->lock reentrancy handoff plus the worker_thread idle-sleep transition without claiming live enqueue or wake ownership.
The bridge now audits try_to_grab_pending() and the __queue_work() pwq->refcnt retry seam so the pending ownership window is recorded without claiming live submission control.
The bridge now records queue_delayed_work_on() and __queue_delayed_work as delayed submission aliases over timer-backed queueing instead of new execution ownership.
The bridge records delayed_work_timer_fn() as the timer-base handoff back into __queue_work() without claiming runtime timer ownership.
The bridge keeps mod_delayed_work_on() review-only by naming CPU affinity, timer-base state, and immediate queueing fallthrough as C-owned governance.
The bridge keeps __flush_workqueue() and drain_workqueue() review-only by naming work_color, flush_color, and flusher coordination as C-owned governance.
The bridge records rescuer_thread(), wq->maydays, pwq->mayday_cursor, and wake_up_worker() so mayday rescue stays explicit and review-only.

The bridge now records wq_worker_running(), wq_worker_sleeping(), WORKER_NOT_RUNNING, and pool->nr_running so scheduler-visible worker-state transitions stay explicit and review-only under the live pool lock.

Live worker_pool execution, scheduler parity, rescuer ownership, delayed-work requeue control, runtime max_active retuning, and hotplug-driven migration remain blocked under the existing C implementation because the roadmap and freeze map still keep kernel/workqueue.c in a study-only boundary posture.
